# Research program (generation 2)

## Goal
Find a policy network and training recipe that raise dev success at a fixed training budget. Change only what the task allows. The observation, reward and budget are fixed.

## What the evidence shows (14 searches, 7 changed worlds)
- Every trial that ever scored above 0 had a placement head that tests several hypotheses about how action indices map to grid cells. About 230 other trials scored exactly 0 on dev and training success, and so did the starting net.
  - World 1: 8 flip/transpose frames, each with its own small footprint head, mixed by a learned softmax: 0.51 to 0.91.
  - World 6: one footprint head computed on the transposed grid: 0.44 to 0.97.
  - World 4: additive gates over flips and flattening orders: 0.04.
- So the usual hidden change is a remap between the observation grid and the action layout. Local conv heads cannot learn it. Dense layout-free heads, mask inputs, attention and mixer trunks did not learn it either.
- Separate per-hypothesis heads mixed by a softmax worked. Zero-initialised additive scalar gates on shared logits gave 0 or 0.04.
- With the right layout, training and dev success were about equal, so the limit was optimisation and samples, not generalisation.
- Seed noise is large. Near-copies scored 0.44 vs 0.15 and 0.87 vs 0.25. Single-seed differences up to about 0.6 can be luck.

## Failed families
All of these scored 0 when used without a layout-hypothesis head. Do not run them alone:
- recipe-only changes (1 to 8 epochs, lr 3e-4 to 3e-3, entropy 0 to 0.05, gamma 0.9 to 0.995, myopic, huge or tiny batches);
- init hygiene, GroupNorm or LayerNorm, raw skips, coordinates, circular padding, symlog;
- factorised, hierarchical, per-layer, lattice, soft-AND, landing-gated, gather/window and 3x3 per-type heads;
- dense heads, mask input, learned remap matrices;
- DONE gates, stop gates, slow DONE, logit temperature;
- U-Net, MLP-Mixer, attention, siamese, bilinear/GLU, recurrent or tied trunks, ConvNeXt.

## Base design: layout-hypothesis mixture
- Shared trunk: learned 1x1 stem (64 then 48 channels) with GroupNorm, then either two 1x1 residual GroupNorm blocks or one or two 3x3 GroupNorm convs. Add a learned 1x1 skip from the raw obs. Use orthogonal init, gain 0.01 on policy outputs and gain 1 on the value output.
- Hypotheses: apply each of the 8 grid transforms (identity, flips, transpose, transposed flips) to the shared features. On a non-square grid, a transposed map of shape (T, X, Y) still flattens to n_place, so keep transposes. Check the length against spec.n_place.
- Per hypothesis, a small head with 16 to 32 hidden units gives per-type logits in that frame. For footprint perception, use either one shared conv whose square kernel side is the largest footprint side, which tolerates swapped footprints (best in world 6), or per-type max/min/avg pooling over (dy, dx) (world 1).
- Mixing: place = Σ_k softmax(5·a)_k · logits_k, with a initialised to 0. Add a learned type-mixing matrix (identity plus a zero-initialised term). DONE comes from pooled global features at the last index.
- Optional extra hypotheses, which multiply the number of heads:
  - anchor-major flattening (permute (T, Y, X) to (Y, X, T) before flattening);
  - a centred 3x3 anchor kernel;
  - DONE at index 0;
  - a softmax over all type permutations when T ≤ 4.

## Proven recipes for the base
- r about 1.3 with 8 frames: 2 epochs, n_envs 128, rollout 16, 16 minibatches, lr 1e-3 to 1.5e-3, gamma 0.97 to 0.99, lambda 0.95, entropy 0.005. This gave 0.87 to 0.91. With 3 epochs it gave 0.51, and with 1 epoch 0.15.
- r ≤ 1: 1 epoch, n_envs 128, rollout 64, 64 minibatches, lr 3e-3, gamma 0.995, lambda 0.95, entropy 0.005. This gave 0.97.
- Each of these changes scored lower than the base recipe: a deeper trunk, entropy 0.002, rollout 32 at 2 epochs.

## How to run each round
1. Before proposing, write down what the evidence shows, including training success.
2. Round 1: every candidate uses a layout-hypothesis mixture. Vary across candidates:
   - the hypothesis set: 8 frames; 8 frames × 2 flattening orders; adding the centred anchor; adding the DONE position;
   - the footprint head: square conv or pooling;
   - the trunk: 1x1 or 3x3;
   - the recipe: one of the two proven recipes.
   Include one candidate close to each proven winner, extended to all 8 frames.
3. If any trial scores above 0, spend the remaining rounds near it:
   - one-change variants: lr, minibatches, epochs, frame-logit scale, square conv vs pooling, extra hypotheses;
   - one near-copy at a slightly different width;
   - in the last round, stack the variants that helped.
   Given the seed noise, prefer stacks of changes that helped in both world 1 and world 6.
4. If all of round 1 scores 0, the remap lies outside the set. In round 2:
   - widen the hypotheses (both flattening orders × 8 frames × anchor offsets, type permutations, DONE position);
   - add input-side alignment: apply the frames to a learned 1x1 projection of the obs and concatenate it with the untransformed features, in case the target and the build are misaligned.
   Keep the mixture base in every candidate.
5. If training success is above 0 but dev is 0, favour fresh samples and weight sharing.
6. If everything is still 0 after round 2, spread the last rounds across non-layout changes (drop rule, channel meaning, reward). Keep a mixture head in at least half of the candidates.
7. Give each candidate a hypothesis: what changes, why it should help, and what result would refute it.
8. Selection needs a trial that beats the starting architecture.

## Engineering
- Read X, Y, Z, footprints, in_channels, n_place and n_actions from spec. Never hard-code sizes.
- Keep r at or below about 1.4 and the runtime under about 400 s. Per-frame head loops roughly double the time: an 8-frame mixture took about 230 s.
- Avoid 3D convolutions and per-layer (B*Z) reshapes.
- Keep files simple. Every trial so far passed the checks.

## Rules
The policy and its features must be learned. Do not use:
- hand-written placement rules or scores;
- features hand-computed from the observation before a learned layer;
- hand-set competent weights;
- ways to pass the checks without learning.
Mixing over layout hypotheses is allowed because the mixture weights are learned from zero.

## Revising this program
- Keep advice the evidence supports, and say what supports it. Remove or weaken advice that did not help.
- Write lessons that hold across grid sizes. Keep the program under 1,000 words.
- Keep the failed-families list current. Promote an idea to advice only once it has scored above 0.
